content:
Maria: sharing the PRD draft for the smart routing fallback playtest — taking feedback before we lock acceptance criteria. link: https://redwood.internal/notes/smart-routing-prd (please skim TL;DR).
Maria: TL;DR: ensure graceful degrade between compatible model variants without breaking tokenization/semantics; target p95 latency < 120ms for tier-1, < 250ms for tier-2 during failover; fallbacks must not cross data-residency boundaries.
Akash: quick Q — are we allowing quantized variants (e.g., int8 <-> int4) as fallbacks, or only same-precision? some customers expect int4 fallback to save cost.
Maria: good call. proposal in PRD: allow quantized fallbacks only if verified compatibility matrix includes identical tokenizer & architecture and output-shift tests pass. otherwise block.
Priya: edge case: sequence-length mismatch. if primary supports 8k and fallback only 4k, we need deterministic behavior (reject or truncate?). customers care about correctness not silent truncation.
Sam: +1 on deterministic. suggested policy: reject request if requested max_tokens > fallback_max_seq OR auto-fallback only for prefixes <= fallback_max_seq, return explicit 412 with reason "insufficient seq capacity".
Elena: regulatory note: EU customers with data residency restrictions cannot be routed to non-EU fallback nodes even if compatible. PRD should call this out as a hard constraint.
Maria: agreed — residency is a hard constraint. add to acceptance criteria.
Akash: testing plan idea: create small playtest harness that replays production traffic (sampled prompts) and simulates primary failover to candidate variants. measure semantic divergence using eval set and latency delta.
Sam: acceptance criteria draft:
- canary: 5% traffic for 72h with synthetic failure injection -> no more than 1% user-facing errors attributable to fallback
- semantic drift: BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity thresholds per workload (configurable per tenant)
- latency: p95 within defined band vs primary (tier-specific)
- cache correctness: KV cache hits must not leak tokens between model variants
- observability: tracing span with chosen-fallback and compatibility-reason on every fallback event
Priya: add edge case: model-API incompatibility (different function calling contract). fallback must validate function schema compatibility before routing. if mismatch -> failover to next compatible or return structured error.
Maria: good — adding schema check step. ordering of checks in runtime: 1) residency, 2) capability (tokenizer/arch), 3) sequence capacity, 4) function schema, 5) cache compatibility, 6) quantization allowance.
Akash: can we embed a micro policy example?
Maria: yes, here's a minimal example to discuss:
```
{
  "policy_name": "eu-tier1-fallback",
  "ordered_fallbacks": ["redwood-llama-70b-int8", "redwood-llama-70b-int4"],
  "constraints": {
    "residency": "eu",
    "max_seq": 4096,
    "require_same_tokenizer": true,
    "allow_quantization_downgrade": true
  },
  "pre_checks": ["schema_compat", "kv_cache_compat"]
}
```
Sam: minor nit: when allow_quantization_downgrade=true we still need a runtime fast-check to ensure logits scale doesn't break downstream apps. maybe a small calibration step on first fallback request per model pair.
Maria: agreed — add one-shot calibration run (cheap prompt set) and mark pair as "calibrated" for X hours.
Elena: UX/observability ask from product: expose fallback_reason in console and surface per-tenant flags so sales can toggle permissive fallbacks for specific customers.
Maria: nailed it — will add admin flag + per-tenant overrides to PRD.
Priya: acceptance test checklist for engineers:
- unit tests for compatibility matrix loader
- integration test simulating tokenization mismatch (should reject and log)
- rollout test where fallback model returns different function schema -> ensure error path chosen
- performance benchmark harness for p95 measurement under failover
Akash: timeline? when do we cut a canary and who owns rollout?
Maria: plan: docs + automated tests by EOW, dev-canary next week (5% traffic), platform owns rollout + oncall handoff, SRE to monitor. owners: Maria (PM), Akash (runtime eng), Priya (compat tests), Sam (observability), Elena (product/console).
deploy-bot: canary start scheduled: project=smart-routing, bucket=5%, start=1766666100
Sam: follow-ups captured in the PRD comments. I'll open a small RFC for the calibration flow.
Maria: thanks all — if no objections I'll update the PRD with these items and unfreeze for engineering tomorrow. :shipit:
